payload.vision_scope_stated: Complete. Vision inherited from se.vision by pointer with a one-line delta; to-be world and goal system stated with their conflict named (trunk-cleanliness vs auditability, resolved as nothing-lost-outranks); Moore pitch filled in all five slots; scope is the WRITE side end to end plus the two provisioning gaps; non-goals name eight exclusions and where each went.
payload.problem_agreed: The delta is real and evidenced, not anticipated. A ship reported success and produced ZERO commits (i8c, ten gates passed, trunk HEAD unmoved, 45 files uncommitted). A routine worktree removal would have destroyed four acceptance tests that existed in exactly one directory. A single close put 72 files on trunk, ~57 of them evidence documents the design says must never land there. And a design section written months ago - main holds live claims, branches hold the record - has never had a single line of code behind it. The goal is worth having because the failure mode is silent: the process says shipped, the repository says nothing happened, and nobody notices until the next morning.
payload.prior_art_positioned: Positioned against four alternatives, each shedding something this does not: merge-everything sheds trunk readability; squash sheds the second parent and with it the structural link to the record; delete-at-close sheds auditability; an external evidence store sheds atomicity between record and claims. The design's own ruling (se-v2-design §4) is the two-parent filtered merge, and v1's practice of keeping heavy material out of the live set is the same instinct. Nothing here is novel git; the novelty is only that SE performs it as one mechanical close.
payload.success_measurable: Every need carries a mechanical pass line. Trunk carries live claims only: after a close, git ls-tree on trunk shows no evidence, machines or state.json for that iteration. Nothing is lost: git show iter/<id>:<evidence path> returns a file trunk does not have. Work is durable mid-iteration: after a milestone bless the branch has a new commit and the tree is clean. A false ship is impossible: shipMerge on a branch with zero commits refuses instead of reporting merged. No regression: a closed iteration still appears in the board's iteration list, sourced from the grant index.
payload.risks_logged: Register open with owners and triggers: R1 content loss at the filter (agent; mitigated by tagging BEFORE the filtered commit and refusing if tagging fails), R2 git's memory of a filtered merge (agent; revisit at the second close after this one), R3 dangling pointers (agent; the triple is written before the first filtered close), R4 the grants-on-trunk exception erodes (owner; revisit if the index ever carries content). Carried: worktree provisioning (closed by this iteration), the Windows battery flake (mitigated, deeper root owed), live phone pairing (owner's physical step, untouched).
